# Technical Approach (SEP-2640)

How the Skills Extension uses MCP's Resources primitive.

## Design Choice: Convention Over New Primitive

Six approaches were evaluated [5]. The working group selected Approach 6
("official convention as intermediate step") which became SEP-2640,
submitted April 23, 2026 [3][5].

The rejected alternative (SEP-2076) proposed skills as a distinct MCP
primitive with new `skills/list` and `skills/get` methods. It was closed
in February 2026 after the working group chose convention-based approaches
first [5].

**Rationale:** reuses existing Resources primitive with zero protocol
changes, avoids "complexity fatigue — too many overlapping concepts
(servers, skills, plugins, hooks, agents) erode credibility and
adoption" [5].

## Skill Format

Skills conform to the Agent Skills specification [12] and are served as
MCP Resources [3]:

- **Root file:** `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name` and
  `description` required) [3][12]
- **Supporting files:** optional scripts/, references/, assets/ [12]
- **Directory-based:** each skill is a directory, matching the filesystem
  model [3][12]

## URI Scheme: skill://

```
skill://<skill-path>/SKILL.md
skill://<skill-path>/<file-path>
```

The final segment of `<skill-path>` MUST equal the skill's `name` as
declared in frontmatter [3][10]. This makes skill identity recoverable
from URIs alone without fetching content [3].

**Examples** [10]:
- `skill://git-workflow/SKILL.md` — single-segment skill
- `skill://acme/billing/refunds/SKILL.md` — nested organizational path
- `skill://code-review/references/SECURITY.md` — supporting document

## Discovery Mechanisms

**Optional enumeration:** `skill://index.json` — a well-known index
resource with entries of type `skill-md` (concrete skills) or
`mcp-resource-template` (parameterized namespaces via RFC 6570 URI
templates) [3].

**Direct URI access:** skills are directly readable via standard
`resources/read` with no discovery machinery required [3]. Servers may
direct agents to specific URIs through their `instructions` field [3].

**Enumeration is optional by design:** "A server is not required to make
its skills enumerable" [3]. This accommodates servers with thousands of
generated skills, unbounded catalogs, or template-based skill creation [3].

## Protocol Integration

**Capability declaration** [3]:
```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "extensions": {
      "io.modelcontextprotocol/skills": {}
    }
  }
}
```

**Reading:** standard `resources/read` with no skill-specific semantics [3].
Internal references resolve against the skill's root directory [3].

**Host tool:** hosts should expose a `read_resource` tool enabling models
to load skill content on demand [3].

**Unified treatment:** "Hosts that support both filesystem-based skills and
MCP-served skills SHOULD treat them identically, as though the set of
connected servers' skill:// resources were mounted into a virtual
filesystem" [3].

## Security Model

The specification establishes firm boundaries [3]:
- Skills are **untrusted input** subject to prompt-injection defenses
- **No implicit execution** — hosts must not honor executable mechanisms
  (hooks, scripts, shell commands) without explicit user approval
- **No elevated authority** — skills are instructional data, not
  directives superseding user policy
- **Provenance visibility** — hosts should indicate originating servers

## Key Decisions

| Date | Decision | Rationale |
|------|----------|-----------|
| 2026-02-14 | Instructor format, not helper/executable | Portability, security, MCP alignment [9] |
| 2026-02-26 | Skills-as-resources (not new primitive) | Client helper tools, existing infrastructure [9] |
| 2026-03-16 | Lean _meta namespace | Avoid fragmenting metadata across transport [9] |
| 2026-04-16 | skill:// URI scheme with name in final segment | Identity from URI without content fetch [9] |
| 2026-04-19 | Filesystem as implementation detail | Portability (no filesystem required) [9] |
| 2026-04-19 | Archive distribution permitted | Atomicity, reduced round-trips [9] |

## Backward Compatibility

No new protocol methods, message types, or schema changes [3]. Servers
not implementing the extension simply expose no skill:// resources [3].

## Gaps and Limitations

- SEP-2640 is "In Review" as of May 2026 [13] — not yet accepted into
  the MCP spec
- No MCP client ships native skill:// support yet (skillsovermcp.com
  provides a tool-wrapper shim as a workaround) [14]
- Models "do not reliably load or follow skill instructions, even when
  skills are preloaded" — adherence is "time-decaying" [7]
- Plugin/bundle packaging is explicitly out of scope [13]
